MUQATIL:14:17/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:17/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:17/r1.claim: The damned swallow the drink with great difficulty; “scarcely see it” in 24:40 means they do not see it at all.

MUQATIL:14:17/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:17/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:17/r2.claim: Death approaches from every direction in Hell, but they do not die; after twenty-one thousand years a gate called al-Hayhat opens, and further torment continues without relief.

FARRA:v2p72/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p72/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v2p72/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says الموت comes as punishment from before, behind, right, and left.

FARRA:v2p72/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p72/r2.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
FARRA:v2p72/r2.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi explains يأتيه الموت من كل مكان as coming from every hair.

FARRA:v2p72/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p72/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p72/r3.claim: ميت describes an existing state, while مائت or ميت may describe what will die; Arabic uses the same present-state versus future-quality distinction in سيد/سائد and كريم/كارم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p231#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p231#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p231#3/r1.claim: Death reaches every place in the person's body, yet he does not die.

TAB-FULL:v13p617/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p617/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p617/r1.claim: For each tyrant, Hell is before him; وراء can mean “in front,” as the cited poem uses it.

TAB-FULL:v13p617/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p617/r2.speaker: بعض نحويي أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v13p617/r2.claim: A Basran grammarian explains “before him” as what lies ahead of the present state, since the present is already past behind it; 18:79 uses the same sense.

TAB-FULL:v13p617/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p617/r3.speaker: بعض نحويي أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v13p617/r3.claim: A Kufan grammarian says this use is most common for times, which pass behind a person once experienced.

TAB-FULL:v13p617/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p617/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v13p617/r4.claim: Another grammarian treats وراء as an opposite, able to mean either what is ahead or what is behind.

TAB-FULL:v13p620/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p620/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p620/r1.claim: The damned sip the drink and can hardly swallow it because of its repulsiveness, yet thirst makes them swallow it.

TAB-FULL:v13p620/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p620/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p620/r2.claim: Arabic uses لا يكاد both for something that happens, as here, and for something that does not, as in the verse about failing to see one’s hand.

TAB-FULL:v13p620/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p620/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v13p620/r3.claim: The Prophet says that this drink cuts the drinker’s intestines until they exit through the anus.

TAB-FULL:v13p620/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p620/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v13p620/r4.claim: The same report links this punishment to boiling water that cuts bowels and to molten liquid that scorches faces.

TAB-FULL:v13p621/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p621/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p621/r1.claim: Death presses from every direction and every bodily part, but the sinner neither dies and rests nor lives in a way that brings relief because the soul is trapped at the throat.

TAB-FULL:v13p621/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p621/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p621/r2.claim: Mujahid says the soul hangs at the throat, neither leaving so the person dies nor returning to the body to restore ease.

TAB-FULL:v13p621/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p621/r3.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
TAB-FULL:v13p621/r3.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi says death reaches the unbeliever from beneath every hair on his body.

ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p156/r6.claim: Yasīgh means to go down easily; the drinker cannot swallow the fluid, and waraʾahu in the final phrase means after it.

NAHHAS:v2p365/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p365/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p365/r2.claim: Angels force the damned to swallow the drink; it barely passes the throat, death comes from every bodily place, and another torment may follow.

THALABI:v5p310/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p310/r10.claim: He is not dead, so he cannot release his soul and rest.

THALABI:v5p310/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
THALABI:v5p310/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the soul remains at the throat, unable to leave and cause death or return to the body and restore life.

THALABI:v5p310/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p310/r12.claim: The final phrase means another severe punishment awaits after this torment.

THALABI:v5p310/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p310/r2.claim: The condemned swallows the drink in repeated gulps rather than one, because of its bitterness and heat; لا يكاد يسيغه means he can scarcely swallow it.

THALABI:v5p310/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p310/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says they do not like the drink; another view says the same.

THALABI:v5p310/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r4.speaker: أبو أمامة
THALABI:v5p310/r4.claim: Abu Umama transmits a Prophetic report: when the drink nears the condemned, it burns his face and scalp, then severs his intestines as he swallows it.

THALABI:v5p310/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p310/r5.claim: The text links the hot drink severing intestines and the burning of faces to other Qur'anic descriptions.

THALABI:v5p310/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p310/r6.claim: Death's pain and illness come to the condemned from every limb or place.

THALABI:v5p310/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r7.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
THALABI:v5p310/r7.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi says the pain reaches from beneath every hair on the body.

THALABI:v5p310/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r8.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v5p310/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak locates the pain even in the big toe.

THALABI:v5p310/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p310/r9.speaker: الأخفش
THALABI:v5p310/r9.claim: Al-Akhfash says death here names the torments that afflict the unbeliever in Hell.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r3.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r3.claim: Death comes from every part of the body's painful extremities, even the tips of the hair.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r4.claim: Causes of death approach from every direction, above, below, front, back, right, and left.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r5.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r5.claim: Alternatively, death's agonies and hardships come to him from every direction.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r6.claim: He does not die so that death's agonies and its prolonged throes continue, increasing his punishment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p128/r7.claim: The following phrase repeats the earlier explanations of من ورائه, and the heavy punishment is eternal residence in Hell.

QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r6.claim: The punishment feels like death in every limb, time, and place, but the people of Hell do not die; the thick punishment is eternal residence there.

QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r7.claim: This is the outcome for those deceived by a few easy days who failed to prepare for what follows.

QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p119/r8.claim: The works of disbelievers vanish like ash in a storm, leaving them ruined in both worlds.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r1.claim: Tajaraʿa describes taking a drink in successive, reluctant sips; Ibn Abbas glosses it as drinking under compulsion.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r2.claim: The commentary refers back to its earlier explanation of kada in the verse about lightning almost taking sight.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r3.claim: Sāgha means that a drink passes smoothly down the throat; the cited verse of al-Farra uses the verb for a drink going down.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r4.claim: His cited poem uses sāgha for a drink that goes down smoothly.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r5.claim: They say the condemned drink it in sips because of its bitterness, and treat kada as redundant, so the phrase means he cannot swallow it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r6.claim: He glosses the inability to swallow as not getting the drink down.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p433/r7.claim: They read the phrase as swallowing only after delay; Arabic ما كدت أقوم can mean that one eventually stood after a delay, so kada is not redundant.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r1.claim: In the darkness verse, the context already proves that the person did not see, so kada there can be an emphatic addition.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r2.claim: The reference to the drink melting what is inside the stomach presupposes that some of it was swallowed; the repeated sipping also signals that some goes down, making total inability to swallow implausible.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r3.claim: He reconciles the wording by taking the negation to mean that the drinker cannot swallow all of the drink, although he swallows some.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r4.claim: Alternatively, swallowing can imply willing acceptance and relish; the unbeliever sips in disgust and cannot drink the liquid readily in one gulp.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p435/r5.claim: Both explanations can preserve the commentators' redundant reading of kada, but the interpretation that does not make kada redundant is stronger.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r1.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r1.claim: One analysis supplies an omitted word: the agony and distress of death reach him, since death itself cannot arrive while he remains alive.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r2.claim: A second analysis takes death as deathlike misery and affliction: the unbeliever is figuratively dead while still breathing, a sense also attributed to al-Akhfash.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r3.speaker: الحديث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r3.claim: A report calls poverty the greatest death, supporting figurative use of death for severe misery.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p436/r4.claim: The cited poet says that one who dies and rests is not truly dead, but the miserable living person is; the lines support the figurative sense.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r1.claim: He explains that death reaches the condemned from every hair on his body.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r2.speaker: الثوري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r2.claim: He says death comes from every vein; most commentators likewise take the places to be parts of the body.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r3.claim: In another report, death comes at him from every direction: right, left, above, below, front, and behind.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r4.claim: He takes waraʾ here to mean in front of the condemned on the Day of Resurrection.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r5.claim: He reads the next punishment as coming after the pus drink; Abu Ishaq and Abu Bakr prefer this sense and paraphrase it as what follows that ordeal.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p438/r6.claim: A thick punishment means pains joined together and multiplied, like a thick thing whose parts have accumulated; compare the description of great punishment.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r2.claim: He sips the bitter drink gradually and can barely swallow it except with difficulty.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r3.claim: Causes of death assail the unbeliever throughout his body, even every hair, yet he does not die and lose consciousness of life.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:16-18/r4.claim: More intense, continuous pain follows this torment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r1.claim: The condemned person drinks the bitter, hot liquid one sip at a time rather than all at once.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r2.claim: Yakādu is an addition here, so the sense is that he cannot swallow it, as in the verse about the mirage.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r3.claim: He glosses yusīghuhu as getting it down.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that he can scarcely swallow it, and it boils inside him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p341/r5.claim: Abu Umāma reports that the drink burns the face and scalp, cuts the bowels, and passes through the body.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r1.claim: Death's anguish and pain reach the unbeliever from every part of his body.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r2.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r2.claim: He says the pain reaches even from beneath every hair on the body.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r3.claim: Another view has death coming from every direction: front, back, above, below, right, and left.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r4.claim: He is not dead, and so cannot rest.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r5.claim: His soul remains caught at his throat, neither leaving to die nor returning to restore life.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p342/r6.claim: Waraʾahu again means ahead; the following punishment is severe, or, by another view, eternal residence in Hell.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r10.speaker: الفضيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r10.claim: Al-Fuḍayl says the continuing thick punishment is the severing and trapping of breaths inside bodies.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r8.claim: Yataj arrʿuhu means he forces himself to swallow; kāda intensifies the phrase to mean he scarcely approaches being able to swallow it, linking to 24:40.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p512#2/r9.claim: Death's approach from every direction means all forms and causes of death surround him; alternatively, it reaches every part of his body, even a toe or every hair root.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r3.claim: The description of swallowing it and barely getting it down conveys how difficult the drink is to bear.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r4.claim: A report depicts the drink scorching the face and making the scalp fall before it cuts the drinker’s intestines.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r5.claim: Death approaches the condemned from every hair on his body, according to Ibrahim al-Taymi, or from all six directions; he is not released by dying.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r6.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r6.claim: Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ explains the severe punishment as holding breath inside the bodies.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p331/r7.claim: The final pronoun in مِن ورائه can refer back to the preceding punishment.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:17-18/r2.claim: The condemned person drinks the pus in repeated sips and can scarcely swallow it: its heat and stench repel him, but he is forced to drink.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r3.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
TABRISI:14:17-18/r3.claim: Death’s agonies reach every part of the body, inside and out, even the tips of the hair.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TABRISI:14:17-18/r4.claim: Death’s agonies reach every part of the body, inside and out, even the tips of the hair.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:14:17-18/r5.claim: Alternatively, death confronts him from every direction and takes him from above, below, both sides, before, and behind.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r6.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:14:17-18/r6.claim: Alternatively, death confronts him from every direction and takes him from above, below, both sides, before, and behind.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:17-18/r7.claim: Despite death’s causes and torments, he does not die and find relief, as in the verse about the people of Hell not being made to die.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:17-18/r8.claim: The punishment behind him is eternal residence in the Fire.

TABRISI:14:17-18/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17-18/r9.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:14:17-18/r9.claim: Alternatively, after the punishment already described comes a still more severe and painful punishment.

TABRISI:14:17/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:17/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:17/r1.claim: The phrase لا يكاد يسيغه describes something not readily swallowed; in لم يكد يراها, the intended meaning is that the person did not see it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r1.claim: Yatajarraʿ means drinking one sip at a time, rather than all at once, because the drink is loathsome and forced upon the drinker.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says yusīghuhu means he cannot swallow it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة عن رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r3.claim: Abu Umama reports that the drink scorches the face and makes the scalp fall when brought near, then cuts the drinker's intestines until it exits through the anus.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r4.claim: Ata transmits that death comes from every hair on the person's body.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r5.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r5.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says death comes from every vein.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj pictures the soul caught at the throat, unable to leave and die or return to its place and find relief.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r7.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas takes “from every place” as every direction: above, below, right, left, behind, and ahead.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r8.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p353/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash says the afflictions that strike the unbeliever in Hell are called death.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354/r1.claim: “He is not dead” means he does not undergo a death that ends life.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sa'ib interprets “after it” as after the pus punishment.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354/r3.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p354/r3.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi says the severe punishment comes after abiding in Hell; ghaliẓ means severe.

RAZI-FULL:v19p82#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p82#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p82#2/r1.claim: One explanation of the next punishment is that it lasts without end.

RAZI-FULL:v19p82#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p82#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p82#2/r2.claim: Another explanation is that each new punishment the condemned faces is more severe than the one before.

RAZI-FULL:v19p82#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p82#2/r3.speaker: المفضل
RAZI-FULL:v19p82#2/r3.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal explains the severe punishment as cutting off breaths and holding them in the bodies.

RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r1.claim: Tajarruʿ means taking a drink gulp by gulp continuously; sāgha means to pass down the throat, and asāghahu means to make it go down.

RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r2.claim: One reading takes negating yakādu idiomatically as affirming delayed success: he eventually swallows it after difficulty, like the idiom ما كدت أقوم and Q 2:71.

RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r3.claim: The cited melting of stomach contents and skins in Q 22:20 also supports eventual swallowing; repeated sipping in يتجرعه suggests some portion goes down.

RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r4.claim: The alternative takes yakādu as near or almost: he does not even come close to swallowing it, as in Q 24:40.

RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r5.claim: The alternatives can be reconciled by saying he does not swallow all of it, or that some reaches his stomach without true swallowing because he takes it unwillingly and cannot tolerate its taste.

RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p82/r6.claim: Causes of death surround the condemned from every direction, or affect every part of his body, yet he does not die.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes waraʾ in 2:91 as meaning something other than what preceded; Abū ʿUbayda says it means what comes after.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r3.claim: Waraʾ may instead mean in front of, supported by several poems and by the description of the king ahead of the people in 18:79; Abū ʿUbayda and Quṭrub adopt this sense.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r4.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the word through idioms: something behind you will come to you, and being behind someone means pursuing him.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r5.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r5.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says waraʾahu means in front of him, not as a true antonym, but because what is hidden is concealed from view.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r6.speaker: الأزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r6.claim: Al-Azharī and also Abū ʿUbayda treat waraʾ as an antonym meaning either behind or in front, both rooted in concealment; Ibn al-Anbārī's explanation that Hell is hidden is judged good.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r8.speaker: أبو أمامة
QURTUBI-FULL:14:16-17/r8.claim: Al-Qurṭubī cites a report from Abū Umāma, from the Prophet, concerning the verse about being given pus to drink and gulping it; the report continues in the next discussion.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r1.claim: Other explanations say God creates pains in the body each like the pain of death, or that the death pangs are prolonged to increase torment.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r2.claim: The suggestion that this implies he dies is wrong: 35:36 says they are not made to die or relieved, and the unbelievers remain perpetually seized by deathlike agonies.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r3.claim: In the closing phrase, min warāʾihi means ahead of him, and ʿadhāb ghalīẓ is severe, continuous pain without respite, like the force meant in 9:123.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r4.speaker: فضيل بن عياض
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17#2/r4.claim: Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ glosses the coming grievous punishment as restraint of breath.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r1.claim: Yatajarraʿuhu means repeatedly sipping it in gulps because it is bitter and hot; the verb forms for gulping are related.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r10.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r10.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the unbeliever does not die and obtain relief.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r11.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the soul remains caught in the throat, neither exiting so he dies nor returning to the body to restore life; he links this to 20:74.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r2.claim: Yusīghuhu means swallowing smoothly; yakādu indicates that he manages it only after delay, as in 2:71 and 22:20, which show eventual swallowing.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets lā yakādu yusīghuhu as being unable to get the drink down or have it pass.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the causes of death reach the unbeliever from every direction, above and below and in front and behind, like the fire's canopies in 39:16.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r5.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r5.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Taymī says death reaches every part of his body, even the ends of his hair, because every part hurts.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r6.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says death comes from every direction and place, even from the big toes.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r7.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash says the term death refers to the calamities inflicted on the unbeliever in Hell, among the greatest forms of death.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r8.claim: Another explanation says each body part faces a kind of torment that would be worse than dying repeatedly, listing bites, stings, fire, chains, boiling water, and other punishments.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:14:17/r9.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says the unbeliever experiences repeated deaths on seeing, approaching, and drinking the requested beverage, so death reaches him without his dying.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r1.claim: He forces himself to swallow the water; it is either an adjective for water or a circumstantial clause with the pronoun in يسقى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r2.claim: He can scarcely swallow it, choking and prolonging his torment; sugh means a drink passing the throat easily and willingly.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r3.claim: Death reaches him from every direction through overwhelming afflictions; alternatively, every part of his body suffers, even hair roots and toe.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r4.claim: He does not die and find relief; ahead of him is continually a torment more severe than his present one.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r5.claim: The thick torment is interpreted as remaining eternally in Hell.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r6.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r6.claim: A second interpretation of the thick torment is breath being withheld.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r7.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:17/r7.claim: Another view detaches the verse from the messengers' story: Meccans sought rain after drought, were denied, and were promised Hell's pus instead.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r1.claim: He drinks the foul liquid in successive gulps but can scarcely swallow; lā yakādu means he does not even approach swallowing, as in 'he scarcely saw it.'

NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r2.claim: Death's causes come from every direction or every part of his body; the expression depicts terrible pain, each part of which would kill if death were possible.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r3.claim: He is not dead because death would bring relief; every future moment brings a punishment heavier than the last.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r4.speaker: الفضيل
NASAFI-FULL:v2p226#6/r4.claim: Al-Fuḍayl says the severe punishment is cutting off the breaths and holding them in the bodies.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r1.claim: Yatajarraʿuhu means that he forces himself to swallow it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r10.claim: The statement that the drinker is not dead refers to the prolonged severity and duration of death's agonies.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r11.claim: He takes the next punishment as ever-facing and progressively harsher at each moment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r12.speaker: الفضيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r12.claim: He interprets the thick punishment as cutting off and constraining breaths inside bodies.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r13.claim: One opinion makes the pronoun in ‘behind it’ refer to the preceding punishment, rather than to every tyrant.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r2.claim: The apparent sense of lā yakādu yusīghuhu is that he does not even come close to swallowing it; if that approach is absent, swallowing itself is absent.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r3.claim: The comparison with ‘he almost did not see it’ explains that denial of near occurrence entails denial of occurrence.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r4.claim: If the quoted report ‘then he drinks it’ is sound, the meaning is that he nearly cannot swallow it before eventually drinking, as the slaughtered cow was nearly not slaughtered before it was done.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r5.claim: The form tajarraʿa may express following an action, effort, doing something gradually, or the same meaning as the simple verb.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r6.claim: Yatajarraʿuhu can syntactically modify the preceding phrase, be circumstantial from the pronoun in yusqā, or stand as a new sentence.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r7.claim: Death coming from every place means its causes; apparently it comes from the six directions, intensifying the terrible suffering.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r8.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r8.claim: He explains ‘from every place’ as from every part of the body, even the tips of its hair; another report extends it to the big toes.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p419/r9.claim: The passage apparently describes the Hereafter; al-Akhfash's reading of worldly afflictions metaphorically called death is unlikely because the context concerns Hell.

SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r1.claim: يتجرعه may modify ماء, be circumstantial to the pronoun in يسقى, or stand independently.

SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r2.claim: تجرع may be the result of جرعته, mean effortful gulping (al-Zamakhshari), indicate gradual sips, or equal simple جرع.

SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes تجرع as effort: the drinker struggles to swallow it.

SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r4.claim: Another sense is gradual sipping, like understanding something bit by bit.

SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r5.claim: It may also equal simple جرع, like عدوت الشيء and تعديته.

SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r6.claim: ولا يكاد يسيغه means he does not even nearly swallow it, so actual swallowing is further away.

SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:17/r7.claim: The pronoun in ومن ورائه عذاب غليظ most clearly returns to كل جبار; another view returns it to the earlier عذاب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p484#3/r4.claim: Abu Umama's report says the drink burns the face and scalp when brought near and cuts the drinker's bowels until they exit; it cites 47:15 and 18:29.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r1.claim: The sinner swallows the drink unwillingly and with difficulty, forced to take it even by an angel striking him with an iron mallet; 22:21 also mentions iron hooks.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r2.claim: He can scarcely swallow because of the drink's bad color, taste, smell, and unbearable heat or cold.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r3.claim: Death seems to approach from every direction, meaning pain reaches the entire body; Maymun says every bone, vein, and nerve, while Ikrima and Ibrahim al-Taymi include every hair.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir interprets death as coming from before, behind, both sides, above, below, and all bodily members.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p485/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says every kind of punishment would cause death if death were possible, but the sinner cannot die; Ibn Kathir explains this as the means of enduring the punishment forever, citing 35:36.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p486/r1.claim: After this suffering comes another punishment, painful, severe, and even worse; the damned alternate between eating Zaqqum, drinking boiling water, and being returned to Hell, as several other passages describe.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r4.claim: The sinner swallows the foul drink only with great effort, in small gulps, because of its bitterness and heat; swallowing it means letting it pass through the throat.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p178/r5.claim: Death-like causes beset him from every direction, but God keeps him alive so the punishment continues; another severe punishment awaits afterward or on Judgment Day.

DURR-FULL:v5p16/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says death reaches the condemned through every kind of torment; each would cause death were God to decree it, but He does not let them die.

DURR-FULL:v5p16/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r2.claim: Mujahid pictures the condemned person's soul caught at the throat, neither leaving to die nor returning to bring relief.

DURR-FULL:v5p16/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r3.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r3.claim: Maimun ibn Mihran says death reaches every bone, vein, and sinew.

DURR-FULL:v5p16/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says death reaches every organ and joint.

DURR-FULL:v5p16/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r5.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r5.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi says death reaches every hair's place on the body and glosses the ensuing severe punishment as eternal duration.

DURR-FULL:v5p16/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r6.speaker: فضيل بن عياض
DURR-FULL:v5p16/r6.claim: Fudayl ibn ʿIyad glosses the severe punishment as being held without breath.

BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r1.claim: ‘He gulps it’ answers an implied question; the verb conveys forced effort and repeated sips driven by thirst and heat because the drink is bitter and foul.

BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r2.claim: He can scarcely swallow it and chokes, enduring prolonged torment sip after sip; smooth passage down the throat is what ‘easy to swallow’ means.

BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r3.claim: A report describes the drink scorching the face and making the scalp fall as it nears; when swallowed, it cuts the intestines until they emerge from the anus.

BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r4.claim: Death comes from every direction as the causes of suffering, from all six sides or every part of the body; any one pain would be fatal if death were possible, but the person remains alive.

BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r5.claim: ‘Behind him’ means ahead of him, after the pus; the next punishment is an ever thicker torment beyond what he has experienced.

BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r6.claim: Al-Kashifi says each succeeding moment brings a more severe punishment, correcting any assumption that torment eases over time.

BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r7.speaker: الفضيل
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r7.claim: Al-Fudayl describes the punishment as cutting off breath and confining it in bodies, which explains why crucifixion is among the severest punishments.

BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p269#2/r8.claim: The text mentions relief from punishment for Abu Lahab and Abu Talib; Abu Lahab freed his nurse Thuwayba after she announced Muhammad’s birth and receives a little water in Hell on Mondays.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows يتجرعه to modify ماء, to be circumstantial, or to begin a new sentence.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r10.claim: The reading يسيغه has a damma on yāʾ because both ساغ الشراب and أساغه غيره are used, with the latter the more eloquent form.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r11.claim: The clause لا يكاد is circumstantial of the drinker's subject, its object, or both.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r12.claim: Death arriving from every place means its causes and ordeals surround the person, expressed figuratively or with an omitted noun.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the approach of death from every place as its surrounding the person on all sides.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r14.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r14.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi says the torment reaches every body part, even the tips of the hair; similar reports are attributed to Maymun ibn Mihran and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r15.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r15.claim: Al-Akhfash takes the phrase as severe worldly calamities for disbelievers, called death by way of exaggeration; al-Alusi considers this remote in the Hell context.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r16.claim: The threatened death is in the afterlife, but the person is not actually dead and so cannot escape the torments.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan allows يتجرعه as a circumstantial clause describing the subject of يسقى.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r3.claim: The independent-sentence reading is strongest: an implicit question asks what is done with the drink, and the answer is that the person repeatedly forces it down.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r4.claim: He gulps the drink repeatedly because thirst and heat overwhelm him.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r5.claim: He can scarcely swallow it and chokes, prolonging torment through both heat and thirst and the painful, slow drinking.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r6.claim: Suugh is the easy passage of a drink down the throat with willing acceptance; negating it denies both ease and acceptance.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r7.claim: The verb may be read as the passive response to جرعه, or as equivalent to the simple verb جرعه.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r8.claim: A further interpretation takes swallowing as getting the drink into the stomach, before the drinker finally drinks it, like the wording about the cow in 2:71.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r9.speaker: أبو أمامة عن النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p202/r9.claim: The Prophet describes the drinker's face being scorched and scalp coming off as the drink nears, then the drink cutting his intestines until it exits below; al-Hakim grades the report authentic.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says the pronoun in وراء refers to the torment already mentioned, rather than to each tyrant.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r2.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r2.claim: Al-Tabrisi identifies the further, severe torment as everlasting residence in Hell.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r3.speaker: الفضيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r3.claim: Al-Fudayl explains the torment as breath being cut off and imprisoned in bodies.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r4.claim: The further torment comes at each turn and is harsher than the preceding one, preventing any assumption that habituation makes it easier.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari suggests the passage from واستفتحوا through this verse may instead address Meccans seeking rain during famine after the Prophet's supplication, promising them pus in Hell instead of rain.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p203/r6.claim: On that proposal, the opening waw is best taken as resumption because the earlier antecedent is distant and nothing restricts the request for victory to a request for rain.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r5.claim: تجرع is effortful swallowing; يسِيغه means make it pass smoothly, and لا يكاد يسيغه means he scarcely approaches swallowing it, much less succeeds, as in Q 2:71.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r6.claim: Death coming from every side means its pains and throes arriving; Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm's verse illustrates death's arrival, and “he is not dead” shows he cannot rest.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p210/r7.claim: The final “behind him is a harsh punishment” repeats the earlier image: another punishment awaits after the one he is already enduring.

TABATABAI:14:15-18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:15-18/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:15-18/r6.claim: Ṣadīd is liquid pus from a wound; tarajjuʿ means swallowing repeatedly sip by sip, and isāgha means letting a drink pass easily through the throat.

TABATABAI:14:16-17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:16-17/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:14:16-17/r4.claim: Al-Ṣādiq explains the ṣadīd of Hell as blood and pus from the private parts of prostitutes in the Fire.

TABATABAI:14:16-17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:16-17/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:14:16-17/r5.claim: Abu Umāma transmits the Prophet’s account that the drink is brought near, burns the drinker’s face and scalp, and tears the intestines; Abu Nuʿaym is said to have authenticated the report.

TABATABAI:14:16-17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:16-17/r6.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:14:16-17/r6.claim: A version in al-Qummī adds that the drinker’s bowels are torn beneath his feet and a valley of pus flows out of him.

ASAD-NOTES:14:13#n23/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:13#n23/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:13#n23/r1.claim: The phrase about hardly swallowing means the drinker is trying to reconcile himself to the suffering.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Verses 5–17 present Moses and other messengers facing hardship, persevering, and ultimately prevailing; the Prophet and companions should persist first and show gratitude in the final phase.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The section is generally phrased but addresses Muslims, assuring them that messengers endured severe hardship, even exile, yet believers ultimately succeed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The verses describe the afterlife punishment awaiting the rebellious.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:15/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:15/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:15/r1.claim: When opponents denied religious freedom and tried to force prophets back to their religion, the prophets sought God’s help and victory; God aided them and destroyed the arrogant tyrants, while Hell still awaits those rulers with the punishments described.

STUDYQURAN:14:16/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r6.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r6.claim: He gulps the liquid because it is bitter and hot.

STUDYQURAN:14:16/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r7.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r7.claim: He can scarcely swallow because he chokes on the liquid.

STUDYQURAN:14:16/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r8.speaker: R, Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:14:16/r8.claim: Torment affects every part with pains that cause death, but does not kill him; death would otherwise release him from torment.

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r10.claim: Ingratitude for God’s many blessings typifies those who lose in the Hereafter.

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r7.claim: Another theme is the terrible nature of divine chastisement in this world and the next.
